name: Stern ramp and door
what it is: One leaf, 11 m long and 9.4 m wide, a box girder 0.42 m deep, about 55 t. Raised, it is the stern door: it lies against a rubber seal round the opening; ten cleats hold it, and a safety latch on each door post that needs no oil. It turns on six hinges at the sill and lowers aft onto the quay: level at 90 degrees, and 4 degrees further for a quay that lies lower. Clear driveway 8 m, between the two cylinders.

name: Ramp hinges
what it is: Six along the sill: at each a lug of the ship stands out of the transom into a slot in the leaf's foot, and one pin of 90 mm goes through all of them. The hinge line lies 45 mm abaft the transom and 15 mm under the main deck, so that the roadway comes down level with the deck.

name: Ramp cylinder, port
what it is: Double-acting, bore 300 mm, rod 170 mm, stroke 3.40 m. Hung from a bracket under the upper deck's web beam at 3.6 m and pinned to a lug on the leaf 2.2 m from the hinge: 4.73 m between its pins with the ramp raised, 7.87 m with it level. It pulls: at most 952 kN, 198 bar on its rod side. A load-holding valve is bolted to it: if a hose bursts the ramp stays where it is.

name: Ramp cylinder, starboard
what it is: Double-acting, bore 300 mm, rod 170 mm, stroke 3.40 m. Hung from a bracket under the upper deck's web beam at 3.6 m and pinned to a lug on the leaf 2.2 m from the hinge: 4.73 m between its pins with the ramp raised, 7.87 m with it level. It pulls: at most 952 kN, 198 bar on its rod side. A load-holding valve is bolted to it: if a hose bursts the ramp stays where it is.

name: End flaps
what it is: 8 flaps of 1.1 by 1.2 m across the ramp's end, each on its own hinge: they lie on the quay and take up her list. Stowed, they lie folded back over the roadway; they fold out as the ramp comes down.

name: Door seal
what it is: A rubber strip on the transom round the opening's sides and head: the raised ramp is drawn against it by the cleats. The roadway is left flat where it meets it.

name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 1
what it is: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 0.7 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 2
what it is: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 1.5 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 3
what it is: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 3.3 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

name: Bolt cleat, port, No. 4
what it is: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 4.4 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 1
what it is: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 0.7 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 2
what it is: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 1.5 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 3
what it is: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 3.3 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

name: Bolt cleat, starboard, No. 4
what it is: A bolt of 70 mm shot inboard through the door post into a keeper on the ramp, 4.4 m over the deck, by a small cylinder; drawn back 200 mm to let go. A switch on it says when the bolt is home.

name: Hook cleat, port
what it is: At the door's head: an arm on a pivot under a hanger, with a tooth that stands up abaft a pin on the ramp. To let go, its cylinder drops the arm 35 degrees. A switch on it says when it is home.

name: Hook cleat, starboard
what it is: At the door's head: an arm on a pivot under a hanger, with a tooth that stands up abaft a pin on the ramp. To let go, its cylinder drops the arm 35 degrees. A switch on it says when it is home.

name: Ramp control stand
what it is: A steel desk on the main deck beside the door, port side, against the mooring station's wall: whoever works it stands inboard of it with the ramp's foot at the left hand. On the desk: the emergency stop, a start and a stop button for each main pump, and two spring-centred levers, CLEATS (lock, open) and RAMP (raise, lower). On the upstand: two pressure indicators, 0 to 250 bar (SYSTEM: the pumps' pressure; RAMP LINE A: what carries the leaf, 189 bar with it level), eight lamp windows (power on, pump 1 running, pump 2 running, ramp closed, cleats locked, cleats open, oil level, oil temperature), the key switch that gives the control to the stand or to the bridge, lamp test, horn, and the instructions engraved. Interlocked: no lever does anything until a pump runs; the ramp is not lowered until the cleats are open; the cleats are not locked until the ramp is home; the emergency stop trips both pumps and holds the ramp. A beacon on its top is lit while the ramp is neither locked nor landed. Its door opens on the terminals of X1.

name: Junction box of the ramp's switches
what it is: On the port mooring station's wall behind the control stand: the ten cleats' switches, the two latches' and the two door switches are joined here to the stand, to the bridge's door and ramp panel and to the alarm system.

name: Door switch, port
what it is: On the door post: closed by the raised ramp when it is home against its seal. With the ten cleats' and the two latches' switches it makes "ramp closed and locked".

name: Door switch, starboard
what it is: On the door post: closed by the raised ramp when it is home against its seal. With the ten cleats' and the two latches' switches it makes "ramp closed and locked".

name: Safety latch, port
what it is: On the door post at breast height. It needs no oil to hold: an arm on a pivot whose tooth falls by its own weight behind a striker pin on the ramp as the ramp comes home, and stays there. It is lifted 30 degrees to let the ramp go, by a small cylinder on the cleats' let-go line or, with no oil, by pressing down its handle; a pin through arm and bracket secures it for the sea passage. It lets go first and falls in last. A switch on it says when it is home.

name: Safety latch, starboard
what it is: On the door post at breast height. It needs no oil to hold: an arm on a pivot whose tooth falls by its own weight behind a striker pin on the ramp as the ramp comes home, and stays there. It is lifted 30 degrees to let the ramp go, by a small cylinder on the cleats' let-go line or, with no oil, by pressing down its handle; a pin through arm and bracket secures it for the sea passage. It lets go first and falls in last. A switch on it says when it is home.

name: Stern ramp power pack (HPU-R)
what it is: A tank of about 1,500 litres on a drip tray, with the two main pumps and the cleats' pump on its lid, a breather and filler, level and temperature switches. Oil: ISO VG 46, mineral hydraulic oil of high viscosity index, type HVLP (DIN 51524 part 3; ISO 11158 class HV); filled to 1,260 litres with the ramp raised. On its inboard side a level glass with an engraved scale (FILL; RAMP DOWN; LOW, where OIL LEVEL is given; STOP, under which no pump is run): the oil in it falls 9 cm as the ramp is lowered, because the cylinders' rods take their own volume out of the tank, and comes back as it is raised. Beside it a dial thermometer: the oil works at 30 to 55 degrees, OIL TEMP is given at 70. It works the stern ramp and its cleats; the ramp cover over the fixed ramp is to be worked from it too. Operating instruction: JS3-304-M1.

name: Main pump No. 1
what it is: An axial piston pump of variable delivery under a 37 kW motor on the tank's lid: its pressure compensator holds 195 bar, and it delivers what the valves ask for, up to 100 l/min; with every valve in its middle it holds the pressure and delivers nothing. One pump works the ramp at half speed. Its delivery goes through a non-return valve into the pressure block.

name: Main pump No. 2
what it is: As No. 1. With both running the ramp is raised from its lowest in about a minute and a half.

name: Cleat pump
what it is: A small pump under a 4 kW motor: it works the ten cleats, so that they can be locked and let go with the main pumps stopped. It delivers into a block of its own on the lid, with the cleats' relief valve RV2 (160 bar) on it; line S goes from there to the cleat valve.

name: Oil cooler
what it is: An air-blast cooler on the tank's after end: the return line comes down into it and goes on from its other end to the return filter. Its 1.1 kW fan runs from 45 degrees of oil until it is back at 40.

name: Pressure block
what it is: On the tank's lid: the two main pumps' deliveries come into it, each through its non-return valve; on it the pressure filter, the relief valve set to 210 bar, and the system's gauge on its gauge cock. Line P leaves its top for the valve stand.

name: Return filter
what it is: On the lid: the return comes into it from the cooler and goes through it into the tank. 25 micron, with a clogging indicator.

name: Hand pump
what it is: On the tank's inboard side: with no power the cleats and, slowly, the ramp are worked by it through the same valves.

name: Valve stand
pipes: HY-01A HY-01B HY-02C HY-02D HY-03P HY-03T HY-04S
what it is: On the inboard wall: three lever valves with solenoids (the ramp, the cleats, and one for the ramp cover), each worked from the control stand or here by hand (the ramp's and the cleats' levers work on the page: a pump must run); a gauge on a gauge cock for each of the ramp's two lines; a marker on each of the eight lines that leave its top, with its letter and what it does, and two pressure transmitters (PT1 the system, PT2 line A) for the control stand's indicators. The cleats must be free before the ramp's valve can lower it.

name: Stern ramp starter panel (RSP)
what it is: On the hydraulic pump room's forward wall. Its door opens on the isolator, the two star-delta starters, the two direct starters, the control transformer and the terminals.

name: Main switchboard, 690 V
what it is: Nine cubicles in a row 4.5 m long, looking aft into the aisle: two bus sections with a tie and a separate thruster bus, 1600 A bars, 690 V, 60 Hz. From outboard: 1 SG2 (1000 A); 2 DG3 (400 A); 3 DG2 (400 A); 4 T2 (800 A); 5 TIE (1600 A); 6 T1 (800 A); 7 DG1 (400 A); 8 SG1 (1000 A); 9 BT (800 A). Each has its instruments, its air circuit breaker and, behind the lower door (it opens to a tap), the three bars its cables are landed on: every cable comes up through its gland in the platform, is cleated, and has its number on a tag. The generating sets, the shaft generators, the transformers and the thruster are not installed: the board is dead, and its cables end at their glands. The 440 V and 230 V sections, which face it, are drawn (JS8-865 sheet 2) and not built.

name: PSB: place marked
what it is: NOT INSTALLED. Main switchboard, 440 V section: behind the two transformers; her motors other than the thruster. The stern ramp's feeder ends here. Its place is marked on the floor (4.50 by 0.80 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

name: T1: place marked
what it is: NOT INSTALLED. Main transformer No. 1, 690/440 V, 800 kVA: either of the two carries the whole 440 V load. Its place is marked on the floor (1.05 by 1.10 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

name: T2: place marked
what it is: NOT INSTALLED. Main transformer No. 2, 690/440 V, 800 kVA. Its place is marked on the floor (1.05 by 1.10 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.

name: DG1: place marked
what it is: NOT INSTALLED. Diesel generating set No. 1: 320 kW, 400 kVA, 690 V, 60 Hz, 1,800 rpm. Alternator forward. Its place is marked on the floor (1.30 by 3.70 m) with a sign, and the cables that are to be landed on it end here, tagged.
